title: Eighteen Folders and One Missing Seal
subtitle: 文书与档案 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文书与档案（科学与技术·文书与档案）
meta: 主题语境：文书与档案（科学与技术·文书与档案）　|　核心词汇：document　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 document 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the clerk ① filed a document that no officer in the department would have signed, and he said the filing was the whole of the case. The ② document, meaning the paper and not the record, ran eighteen folders and stayed unsealed on the desk; a document, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unstamped.

Every ③ document in that folder had the same missing seal at the foot of it, and the ④ document at the end, meaning the one they kept for the archive and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever checked twice. A document, his assistant said, is nine parts checking and one part somebody willing to file; the clerk said the checking is the part that fills eighteen folders.

The keeper meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the document was the whole of the shelf, meaning the record and not the paper. The ⑥ document, meaning the record and not any of that, is the only thing on a shelf that everybody stores and nobody reads; document, she said, is either something you file or the only word that means both a paper and a record. She said the record is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ document had become a line in an index, and the index had become an argument about the missing seal. The ⑧ document of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in September, was one folder and eighteen documents of checking; document, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to check. She said the checking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ document I remember is the one at the end, which was sealed in 1974 and is still described as the strangest in the folder. A ⑩ document, the assistant said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being checked; every document, she said, is a record that has agreed to look like a paper. She said the record was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 文件；公文（指卷宗里归档的那一份）
B. n. 文件（指那张纸本身，与那份档案记录相对）
C. 固定搭配：file a document 归档一份文件
D. n. 文件（指留给档案室用的那一份）
E. n. 文件；文书（抽象总称，指一个卷宗的文书之事）
F. n. 文件（指索引里写到、被编目的那一份）
G. n. 档案；文献记录（指架子上保存的那些材料）
H. n. 档案（抽象总称，指人人收存却无人阅读的那些）

items.q: filed a document that no officer in the department would have signed
The document, meaning the paper and not the record
the document was the whole of the shelf
the document had become a line in an index
The document of the whole thing
A document, the assistant said in 1976

answers.why: file a document 意为“归档一份文件”，1952 年办事员归档了一份部门里没有一位官员肯签字的文件。
document 意为“文件”，指那张纸本身而不是那份档案记录，它在桌上历经十八个卷宗而没有盖章。
document 意为“文件、公文”，指那个卷宗里每一份文件，每一份页脚都缺着同一个印章。
document 意为“文件”，指留给档案室用的那一份，是唯一有人核对过两次的。
document 意为“档案、文献记录”，指架子上保存的那些材料，管理员说这些档案就是那层架子的全部。
document 意为“档案”，指人人收存却无人阅读的那些而不是那张纸本身，是架子上人人都收存、却无人阅读的东西。
document 意为“文件”，指索引里写到、被编目的那一份，到 1960 年这份文件成了索引里的一行。
document 意为“文件、文书”，办事员九月写道，整件事的文书之事是一个卷宗和十八份文件的核对。
document 意为“文件”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1974 年盖章，至今仍被说成卷宗里最奇的一份。
document 为抽象总称，助手 1976 年说，一份文件是唯一会因为被核对而变得更好的东西。
